text.tspan: Option 5 · IPv6 clusters: pod addresses are globally unique, so they can't overlap
EKS cluster A, IP family IPv6
chosen at creation, can't be changed later
(each node gets a /80 prefix from the subnet)
EKS cluster B, IP family IPv6
Every IPv6 address is globally unique, so pod IPs
can never overlap. Security groups and NetworkPolicy
IPv4 still overlaps: a pod calling an IPv4-only address
uses its node's IPv4 (SNAT), so IPv4-only services still need
options 1–3. An IPv4 cluster can't be converted: build a new one.
